title: Does a supply that grows with distance from a rod's birth site (instead of a fixed-radius depletion step) let the heritable Marangoni trait carry distance per cycle, so that selection can raise the share of rods that swim 3 own lengths?
summary: c54's three loops on Q:marangoni-distance-pays found that a depletion disc opened at each split site raises the share of dividing Marangoni rods that swim 3 own lengths to 40-55% (20261027T0725), but fixes distance per cycle near the disc radius for every kind: alone, mar-60 rods are 1.5-2x faster and divide sooner but cover the same 3-3.7 own lengths per cycle as mar 40 (20261027T1005), and mar 60 is not favoured in competition (20261027T0830). A step at a fixed radius pays distance by fixing it. A graded payoff could let the trait's extra speed buy distance rather than time.
experiment: One loop. World: 20261027T0830-c54-distance-pays-competition/world.py. Replace the disc step by a graded field: at each split site, for dep_T, lower the chemostat target by an amount that falls smoothly with distance d from the site (e.g. phi_b - (phi_b - dep_in) exp(-d^2 / 2 L^2), L = 2 and 4 rod lengths), so growth keeps improving the farther a daughter gets. Nothing reads kind, speed or displacement. Assay first as in 20261027T1005 (single-kind mar 40 vs mar 60, mutation off, 2 seeds): pass if mar 60's median D per cycle exceeds mar 40's under the graded field while survival per split is similar. If it passes, run the competition assay and then the challenge design (mar-40 founders, mutation on, identical-event twin, the same loss spread globally). Check first that the grid-scale stripes seen around mar-60 bodies do not change at dt/2.
